translation:
In Dwarka, in Pipaji's temple to the right of the Chhappan Sidi Sakshi Gopal temple, there is a plaque. On the day of Guru Purnima in Samvat 2002, a marble image was installed in place of Pipaji's old clay image; the plaque set below it reads as follows.

"Sant Shri Pipaji, disciple of Ramanandji and a great yogi, lived about 650 years before today. It was the day of Mahodaya Parva. Sant Shri Pipaji, together with his wife Sitaji, eager for the darshan (sacred sight) of Dwarkadhish (the Lord of Dwarka), leapt into the sea. Lord Dwarkadhish and Rukmini kept the two of them with them in the palace for several days. As proof, they placed in their hands the marks of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus. They sent the couple back up from the sea in dry clothes. The Lord said: go and spread bhakti (devotion). If you do not return to the surface, people will think that a devotee, drowned in devotion, died in the sea. It is my boon that whenever you wish, you will be able to have my darshan. This account is from Parijat Ashtapadi, chapter 13."

_Pipa hubat na dariya, kariyo samudri got.
Tinahi moti paiya, andar bahar jot. ||1||_
(Pipaji was not afraid of drowning; he took the plunge into the sea, and there found a pearl whose glow spread everywhere, within and without.)

_Krishna chale pahonchaike, Pipa umalyo neer.
Sita sakhi samip hai, bhigyo nahi cheer. ||2||_
(Having brought Pipaji up out of the water, Krishna then departed; thus Pipaji was rescued from the sea. His companion Sita was beside him, and, like him, her garment too did not become wet.)

Because Pipaji was not afraid of drowning in the ocean and dove into the sea, he obtained the pearl of the vision of God, whose radiance spread everywhere, within and without. Shri Krishna brought Pipaji safely out of the sea and then departed; in this way Pipaji was saved from the water. With him was his wife and companion, Sita, and just like him, her garment too had not become wet.

Sitamata and Pipaji shared one guru: Ramanand Gosai. Ramanand's guru was Shri Raghavanand; his guru was Hariyanand; his guru was Devacharya; and his guru was Shri Ramanuj. It was Ramanujji who gave the garland and tilak (marks of initiation) to husband and wife together, as kul-tarak (redeemer of the family) and kul-shekhar (crown of the family) — giving the garland and tilak to both husband and wife alike. This is attested in Nabha Swami's Bhaktamal, in an account (kavit) about Swami Ramanuj:

_Sahas asya updesh kari jagat udharan jatan kiyo.
Gopur hvai arudh uchcha swar manya uchaaryo.
Sute nar pare jaagi bahutari shravanati dhaaryo.
Titaneu gurudev paddhati bhau nyaari-nyaari.
Kulatarak shishya pratham bhakti vapu mangalkaari.
Kripanpaal karuna samudra Ramanuj sam nahi biyo.
Sahas asya updesh kari udharan jatan kiyo._
(Shri Ramanujacharyaji, an incarnation of the thousand-hooded serpent-lord Shesh Bhagwan, made a great effort to deliver the world by teaching the path of devotion. Climbing up onto the high tower of the temple gate, he proclaimed the mantra in a loud, dignified voice, so that sleeping people rose and woke, and many held it fast in their hearts. From this arose separate traditions, each distinct from the other. Among his disciples, Kulatarakji was foremost — devotion embodied, and a bringer of good fortune. Protector of the humble, ocean of compassion — there has never been another like Ramanuj. He made a great effort to deliver the world by teaching this to the multitude.)

Shri Ramanujacharyaji gave the teaching of the path of devotion (bhakti-marg) and thereby made a great effort to redeem the world. His own guru had given him a mantra with instructions to keep it secret; but Ramanujacharyaji climbed up onto the spire of the temple gateway and proclaimed it aloud, so that all people could hear it. Hearing the sound of the mantra, sleeping people awoke, and seventy-two devotees took it into their hearts on hearing it; from this arose seventy-two different traditions (paddhatis). Among his disciples, Kul-tarakji was foremost, one devoted to the welfare of souls and the very embodiment of devotion. There has never been another like Shri Ramanujacharyaji, the ocean of compassion who sustains the humble and those who take refuge in him.

_Japato harinamani sthane shatgunadhikah.
Atmanam cha punatyuchyair japan shreshthena punati cha._
(Reg. 413, p. 449)
(One who quietly, steadily repeats the Lord's name purifies himself alone; but one who chants it aloud from a high place, as kirtan (hymn-singing), purifies all — the animate and the inanimate alike.)

The revered Yadunath has written, in Litiyu no. 56, page 2, that Jivanji Maharaj gave the name "Ramkabir" alone to those who came to him for refuge: "During my lifetime I have chanted this very name to the fullest extent." Concerning this the saints have said that such devotion cannot fully be expressed in words. But for the sake of the world's welfare, Swami Ramanuj climbed the gopur (temple tower) at night and, in a loud voice, broke his guru's command and cried out the Ram-mantra; he accepted hell as the penalty for the sin of disobeying his guru, but for the world's good he climbed the gopur — the high gateway of the temple — and proclaimed the Ram-mantra aloud. Seventy-two people heard it, and they became the seventy-two siddhas (perfected ones). The revered Yadunath writes this in Litiyu 72, page 7 onward.

As the scriptures on the discipline of kanthi-diksha (initiation with a sacred neck-cord) say, revealing the secret openly does not by itself accomplish the intended result. But saints such as Ramanuj, in whose hearts the welfare of the people dwelled, climbed the main gate (simha-dwar, "lion-gate") and proclaimed the deepest of secret mantras to the whole world. In the same way, just as King Janak set out the bow Tryambak to be lifted at Sita's swayamvar (bridegroom-choice ceremony), Baba Kabir too declared:

_Kabir ki kaman padi hai maidan.
Shoora hoy so khenchle nahi kayarka kaam._
(Kabir's bow lies in the open field. Let the one who is brave draw it — this is not work for a coward.)

Kabirji's command has been proclaimed openly on the field of valor. Whoever has the strength should draw the string of this bow of command — that is, take up the challenge. This can be done only by the brave; it is not work for a coward or a timid person. Just as at King Janak's bow-ceremony even a figure like Ravan met only disappointment, the same holds for those without the right to it. At the time of kanthi-diksha, the one who bestows the kanthi should recite, with an impartial spirit, this sakhi (couplet):

_Kanthi bandi chhodki, lije sharan tumhar.
Das nimitt kachhu bhayo, tum jano kirtar.
Kanthi tilak dharke, graho Ramkabir aadhar.
Das garibi gahi raho, utaro bhavjala paar.
Yah baano Radha Krishnako, guru kripate ded.
Dheerajse dhare raho, kripa kare gurudev._
(O Lord, the kanthi frees one from worldly bondage; keep it in Your protection. This humble servant has only become the instrument for this; it is You, O Lord, who must give it true meaning. O devotee, keep wearing the kanthi and tilak with faith, and take refuge in the name of Ramkabir. Hold fast to humility, and you will cross over the ocean of worldly existence. I give this gift by the strength of the guru's grace, for devotion to Radha-Krishna; hold it with patience, and the guru will surely bless you.)

Just as a bride's father has the right to give her away in marriage (kanyadan), so a parthara (one holding recognized elder-authority within the lineage) has that right for the occasion. In the Uda Bhakt Samaj, every parent, whether or not they hold parthara status, can themselves give kanthi-diksha.

Trikamdas Gordhandas, in his diary of Samvat 2032, page 1, writes a kundali (a verse in the kundaliya form):

_Kardi kaman Kabirki, padi mulak maidan.
Shoora hoy to khinchlo, nahi kayarka kaam.
Nahi kayarka kaam, bhaktajan jo jo jhankhi.
Thai jajo bhakt Prahlad, bansona bhakt hankhi.
Shoor Tulsi sam jagine, Trikam thai jaav Valmiki.
Padi mulak maidan, kardi kaman Kabirki._
(Kabir's bow is stern and hard; it lies in the field for the whole land to see. Let the brave one draw it — it is not work for a coward. Not work for a coward — O devotees, examine yourselves closely: become as courageous a devotee as Prahlad; do not become a defective, worthless devotee. Awaken like the valiant Tulsi[das], and become as great as Valmiki, O Trikam[das]. The bow lies in the field for the whole land — Kabir's bow is stern and hard.)

Kabir's commands are very stern; they have been proclaimed openly, and for the weak they are impossible to fulfill. O devotees, examine this carefully: become devotees as courageous as Prahlad, but do not become worthless like a defective, flawed ox. Like the valiant Tulsi and Tulsidas, awaken and become as great as Valmiki. In this world's arena, Kabir's stern commands stand as a challenge.

The essence of devotion (bhaktasya-saar) — creation formed from the union of raj and virya (the elements of conception) — exists within the traditional four wombs of birth, but its present, manifest portion is distinct from these. And within that portion, free of delusion, creation proceeds along the path of the Word (shabda) — this is the fifth "womb": the creation of devotee-gods, which is faultless. Examples of this have been given above: the first is Rohidas, the second Pipaji, the third Parvatiji. (From Vasana Samagam, page 139.)

Its testimony is this — it fulfills what is sought through the thousand names. After Shri Mahadevji gave this teaching to Parvatiji, she, moved, offered this praise:

_Dhanyasmyanugrahitasmi sanathasmikrita prabho.
Shravinam gopyasahasramupadeshamayo kuru. ||73||_
(O Lord! I have been made blessed and graced by you. I have become fulfilled through this alone — you made me hear the most secret scripture; you have given me a protector, and out of grace have given me the guru's teaching.)

_Ram rameti rameti rame rame manorame.
Sahasranaam tattulyam Ramnaam kuru. ||73||_
(Ram, Ram, Ram — thus I delight in the delightful Ram. O fair-faced one, the single name of Ram is equal to a thousand names. From the Ram Raksha Stotra.)

Mahadevji called Parvati to come and eat. Parvatiji said she would come once she had finished reciting the Vishnu-sahasranama (the thousand names of Vishnu), and that he should eat first. Then Mahadevji spoke the shloka beginning "Ram Rameti..." Having learned the glory of the name of Ram from Mahadevji's own mouth, Parvatiji took up the name of Ram and then ate her meal. This is the teaching Mahadevji gave to Parvati — a sakhi:

_Kabir vrahe virahini aakuli. Virahiniye kiyo pitasu sang.
Betiye putra janmiyo. Jaiso punamchand. ||1||_
(Servant Kabirji says: the individual soul, as a woman named Maya, restless in separation from the Supreme Lord, united with the Supreme Father; and from that union the daughter Bhakti gave birth to an excellent son, like the moon on a night of full sainthood.)

Thus husband and wife are both fashioned by the Supreme Lord himself; therefore there is no fault in their marrying one another, even if they are not yet saints of the Lord. In the same way, if they become disciples of one and the same guru, that too should not be counted as wrong or blameworthy. So Jivandasji, presenting evidence from all these scriptural authorities — the Sahasranama, Vedanta, Puranas, Upanishads, and so on — declared that we today follow the tradition established by Ramanand and the other acharyas. Further, on that path, whoever has the grace of Namdev and Kabirji may follow it, walking the same path in the same way that the great souls (mahapurush) walked before; and again, whoever on that path has the grace of Namdev-Kabirji may proceed on it. If husband and wife have separate, different gurus, then it properly becomes a source of dispute between them in their devotion.

Let us understand how our people have carried on the tradition of devotion to God with regard to the Sahasranama. Jivandasji examined all of this; having scrutinized every point, he established prem-bhakti (loving devotion) and kirtan-bhakti (devotion through hymn-singing) in the Uda Bhakt Samaj.

Inner worship is called antaryaag, and outer worship is called bahiryaag. Bahiryaag, the outer ritual action, has five main parts: 1) japa (repeated recitation of the name), 2) hom (fire-offering), 3) tarpan (offering to ancestors and deities), 4) marjan (purificatory sprinkling), and 5) brahma-bhojan (feeding of holy brahmins). Antaryaag likewise has five parts: 1) patal, 2) paddhati, 3) dharma, 4) strot (stotra, hymn), and 5) naam (name). What "sahasra-patal" and the rest actually are is not important for us, but let us look at them for the sake of knowledge.

Patal: building, through the letters of the mantra that expresses the Devi's form, an extensive mental image of devotion within the network of subtle channels (nadi) of the body.

Paddhati: worshiping the Devi in the heart and other seats (pith) through this mantra-patal by means of five or sixteen ritual offerings — this is called paddhati.

Varma, or kavach (armor): after constructing the patal and paddhati in this way in the channels and in seats such as the heart, then constructing an armor over the gross body using the letters of the chosen mantra (ishta-mantra), and cultivating, through the Devi's many names, a sense of protection for the body — this is called dharma or kavach.

After that, bowing to the Devi at the inner level through short hymns and other secret hymns that keep alive the memory of the Devi's mantra, using names that express, among her many qualities, a thousand qualities worthy of special contemplation. These five parts together make up antaryaag.

Mahadev freed Parvatiji from the whole entanglement of the thousand names through the single name of Ram alone. Therefore Jivanji dispensed with the practices described above, and has written of them here only for the sake of information. (Register no. 19/3, page 504, from Kalyan.)

_Shiv Parvatisu kaha. Ramnaam nij dhyan.
Aur sabahi bhram hai. Tu sat kari sat hi jaan._
(Shiva told Parvati that he himself meditates upon the name of Ram; that, he declared, is the name of Ram alone — everything else besides this is illusion and doubt. Know this to be the real truth.)

_Shri Rameti param japyam tarakam Brahmasangyakam.
Brahmahatyadi-paapaghnamiti vedavido viduh._
(The name Shri Ram alone is the supreme name worthy of japa, the liberating name that gives realization of the Supreme Brahman. Learned knowers of the Vedas have known that even grave sins such as the killing of a brahmin...
